terms.definition: A single task-level request — one motion, one grasp, one pick. Modelled as a subtype of `IntentDataType`. It is what a client submits and what a mission step holds.
One submitted intent, tracked to completion. Modelled as `IntentOperationType`, a Part 10 program instance created per submission.
An ordered sequence of intents submitted and tracked as a unit. Modelled as `MissionType`.
The prefix of released steps. Committed, possibly already executing, and immutable (§7.2).
The suffix of unreleased steps. Provisional, and revisable by `UpdateMission` (§7.2).

A rigid-body placement — three of position and three of orientation — expressed relative to a named frame. Carried by `Pose3DDataType`, whose orientation is a unit quaternion ordered (x, y, z, w) per §5.2.
A named right-handed Cartesian coordinate system a pose is expressed relative to. Frames form a tree through `HasFrameParent`. Modelled as `CoordinateFrameType`.
The origin of a tool frame; the point a motion intent drives to its target. OPC 40010-1 defines no such concept, so `ToolType.TcpFrame` supplies one.
Rounding the corner between two motions rather than stopping on the first one's target. Requested by `BlendDataType`, and by the blending values of `BufferModeEnum`.
How a newly submitted intent relates to the one already executing — abort it, queue behind it, or blend into it. `BufferModeEnum`.
Whether an intent tolerates motion and other intents alongside it. `BlockingModeEnum`.

The exclusive right, held by at most one Session, to submit intents to one controller (clause 8). It is an arbitration mechanism between clients and **not** the single point of control that ISO 10218-2 requires.
An `ExecutionStateEnum` value from which execution does not resume: `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`, or `Retriable`.
The smallest individually testable requirement of this specification. Grouped into facets rather than claimed one by one.
A named, individually claimable set of conformance units — a building block, not a complete claim. Clause 12.2 defines them.
A named set of facets describing one plausible robot Server, claimed by publishing its URI in `Server/ServerCapabilities/ServerProfileArray`. Clause 12.3 defines them.
